title: Preserve raw bytes when hashing mixed-type object arrays
answers: Why does hash_pandas_object raise UnicodeDecodeError for mixed values containing bytes?
How should hash_array handle non-ASCII bytes alongside integers and None?
Why do bytes with trailing NULs hash differently in mixed-type arrays?
body:
Symptom: hash_array and hash_pandas_object raise UnicodeDecodeError on mixed-type object values containing non-ASCII bytes; trailing NULs can also be lost during conversion.
Root cause: pandas/core/util/hashing.py:_hash_ndarray used whole-array astype(str) in its TypeError fallback, which decodes bytes as ASCII regardless of the requested encoding and can alter their contents.
Fix pattern: Copy the object array, identify bytes with isinstance, stringify only non-bytes elements, and pass the resulting array to hash_object_array with the requested hash key and encoding.
Constraints: Apply this conversion in the mixed-type TypeError fallback. Preserve existing stringification of non-bytes values; bytes must hash consistently with non-mixed inputs, including non-ASCII content and trailing NULs, with categorize enabled or disabled (pandas/tests/util/test_hashing.py:test_hash_array_mixed_bytes).
applies: Object-array hashing through _hash_ndarray, including hash_array and hash_pandas_object callers.
